question: What App Service plan tiers are supported for hosting Azure Functions in a dedicated plan?
expected_answer: Basic, Standard, Premium, and Isolated SKUs
source_passage: The dedicated App Service plans supported for function app hosting include Basic, Standard, Premium, and Isolated SKUs

question: Does Azure Functions support Free and Shared tier App Service plans?
expected_answer: No, Azure Functions does not support Free and Shared tier App Service plans
source_passage: Azure functions doesn't support Free and Shared tier App Service plans

question: What setting must be enabled on an App Service plan to prevent the Azure Functions runtime from going idle?
expected_answer: The Always On setting must be enabled
source_passage: You should enable the Always on setting so that your function app runs correctly. On an App Service plan, the Functions runtime goes idle after a few minutes of inactivity

question: How is billing calculated for Azure Functions running on a dedicated App Service plan?
expected_answer: You are billed only for the plan regardless of how many function apps or web apps run in it, not based on function executions
source_passage: You're billed only for the plan, regardless of how many function apps or web apps run in the plan

question: What is an App Service Environment used for when hosting Azure Functions?
expected_answer: It lets you fully isolate your functions and take advantage of higher numbers of instances than a regular App Service plan
source_passage: Running in an App Service Environment (ASE) lets you fully isolate your functions and take advantage of higher numbers of instances than an App Service Plan

question: How can you reactivate an idled Azure Functions app on an App Service plan without enabling Always On?
expected_answer: Send a request to an HTTP trigger endpoint or any other endpoint on the app, or access the app in the Azure portal
source_passage: Send a request to an HTTP trigger endpoint or any other endpoint on the app. Even a failed request should wake up your app. Access your app in the Azure portal

question: What is a Container Apps environment in Azure Container Apps?
expected_answer: A secure boundary around one or more container apps and jobs where the Container Apps runtime manages OS upgrades, scale operations, failover procedures, and resource balancing
source_passage: A Container Apps environment is a secure boundary around one or more container apps and jobs. The Container Apps runtime manages each environment by handling OS upgrades, scale operations, failover procedures, and resource balancing

question: What are the two types of Azure Container Apps environments?
expected_answer: Workload profiles environments (the default) and Consumption only environments (legacy)
source_passage: There are two different types of Container Apps environments: Workload profiles environments (the default) and Consumption only environments (legacy)

question: What plans does a Workload profiles environment support in Azure Container Apps?
expected_answer: Both the Consumption and Dedicated plans
source_passage: Workload profiles environments support both the Consumption and Dedicated plans

question: What plan does a Consumption only environment support in Azure Container Apps?
expected_answer: Only the Consumption plan
source_passage: Consumption only environments support only the Consumption plan

question: When should you use multiple Azure Container Apps environments instead of a single one?
expected_answer: When you want applications to never share compute resources, not communicate via built-in Dapr service invocation, or be isolated due to team or environment usage such as test vs production
source_passage: Use more than one environment when you want two or more applications to: Never share the same compute resources, Not communicate via the built-in Dapr service invocation API, Be isolated due to team or environment usage

question: Where do all container apps within the same Azure Container Apps environment send their logs by default?
expected_answer: To a common Log Analytics workspace
source_passage: All container apps within an environment send logs to a common Log Analytics workspace, making it easier to query and analyze logs across multiple apps

question: After how many days is an idle Azure Container Apps environment automatically deleted?
expected_answer: After 90 days of being idle with no active container apps or jobs running
source_passage: Azure Container Apps environments are automatically deleted if one of the following conditions persists for longer than 90 days: The environment is idle (no active container apps or jobs running in the environment)

question: What types of logs does an Azure Container Apps environment collect by default?
expected_answer: Container stdout and stderr streams, container app scaling events, Dapr sidecar logs if Dapr is enabled, and system-level metrics and events
source_passage: These logs include: Container stdout/stderr streams, Container app scaling events, Dapr sidecar logs (if Dapr is enabled), System-level metrics and events

question: What happens to function code files if you delete the main storage account of an Azure Functions app?
expected_answer: The function code files are deleted and cannot be recovered
source_passage: When you delete the main storage account of the function app, the function code files are deleted and can't be recovered

question: What component in Azure Functions monitors event rates and decides whether to scale out or scale in?
expected_answer: The scale controller
source_passage: Azure Functions uses a component called the scale controller to monitor the rate of events and determine whether to scale out or scale in

question: In the Azure Functions Consumption plan, what is each host instance typically limited to?
expected_answer: 1.5 GB of memory and one CPU
source_passage: Each instance of the Functions host in the Consumption plan is limited, typically to 1.5 GB of memory and one CPU

question: What property controls the log configuration for all apps in an Azure Container Apps environment?
expected_answer: properties.appLogsConfiguration which is used for configuring the Log Analytics workspace
source_passage: properties.appLogsConfiguration: Used for configuring the Log Analytics workspace where logs for all apps in the environment are published

question: What is the minimum billable execution period for the Azure Container Apps Consumption plan?
expected_answer: 1,000 milliseconds
source_passage: The minimum billable execution period for both execution modes is 1,000 ms

question: In Azure Container Apps, what does the Dedicated plan management fee depend on?
expected_answer: You are charged a Dedicated plan management fee if you have one or more dedicated workload profiles in your environment, regardless of the number of applications
source_passage: If you have one or more dedicated workload profiles in your environment, you're charged a Dedicated plan management fee
